meta.title: Ballot Compass candidate data
meta.coverage_note: Seed data was compiled from public reporting and records available through mid-2026. It has not been checked by a human editor. Every position and status is labeled 'Needs verification'. Results of the November 2026 elections, and any statements made after mid-2026, are not yet reflected.
meta.value_scale: 0-4 per issue; see data/issues.json for what each value means. null means no clear position and the issue is left out of that candidate's score.

candidates.name: JD Vance
candidates.current_role: Vice President of the United States
candidates.status_note: Has said he will discuss a 2028 run with President Trump after the 2026 midterm elections.
candidates.bio: Author and former venture capitalist from Ohio, elected to the Senate in 2022 and as vice president in 2024.

abortion.summary: As the 2024 vice-presidential nominee backed leaving abortion law to the states and said a national ban would be vetoed; during his 2022 Senate race had expressed support for national minimum standards.

immigration.summary: Campaigned in 2024 for large-scale deportation of people in the country illegally and has argued for lower overall immigration levels.

israel.summary: Supports continued military support for Israel; has also argued that U.S. and Israeli interests are not always identical.

iran.summary: Defended the June 2025 U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear sites, saying the U.S. was targeting Iran's nuclear program rather than seeking a wider war.

ukraine.summary: As a senator opposed further Ukraine aid and voted against the 2024 supplemental; as vice president has backed a negotiated settlement.

china_trade.summary: Supports broad tariffs as a tool to rebuild U.S. manufacturing and to pressure China and other trading partners.

taxes.summary: Cast the tie-breaking Senate vote in July 2025 to pass the budget law that made the 2017 tax cuts permanent and reduced projected spending.
taxes.source_label: Congress.gov: H.R. 1 (2025), One Big Beautiful Bill Act

healthcare.summary: Supported the 2025 budget law's Medicaid changes, including work requirements; has not offered a separate health plan.
healthcare.source_label: Congress.gov: H.R. 1 (2025), One Big Beautiful Bill Act

guns.summary: Opposes new federal gun restrictions; has emphasized school security in response to shootings.

energy.summary: Favors expanded U.S. oil and gas production and has criticized electric-vehicle mandates and clean-energy subsidies.

ai.summary: At the February 2025 AI Action Summit in Paris, warned against excessive regulation and said the U.S. intends to lead in AI.

education.summary: Has criticized universities and backed school choice in general terms; no clear position on the federal role was found in the seed research.

crime.summary: Publicly supported the 2025 deployment of National Guard troops to Washington, D.C.

democracy.summary: Wrote in February 2025 that judges are not allowed to control the executive branch's legitimate power; opposes Supreme Court restructuring.

candidates.name: Marco Rubio
candidates.status_note: Has said he would support JD Vance if Vance runs; has not ruled out a run of his own.
candidates.bio: Former Florida House speaker and three-term U.S. senator; 2016 presidential candidate.

background.legislative_experience: U.S. Senator from Florida, 2011-2025; Speaker of the Florida House.

abortion.summary: Said during a 2015 presidential debate that he opposed exceptions for rape and incest; has a consistent anti-abortion voting record.

immigration.summary: As Secretary of State has carried out the administration's deportation and visa policies. In 2013 he co-wrote a bipartisan bill that included a path to citizenship.

israel.summary: Long-time strong supporter of Israel; as Secretary of State opposed moves by allies to recognize a Palestinian state.

iran.summary: Long advocated maximum pressure on Iran; supported the June 2025 strikes on nuclear sites.

ukraine.summary: Has called the war a stalemate that must end through negotiation; as Secretary of State has led U.S. talks with both sides.

china_trade.summary: One of the leading China hawks in Congress; supports tariffs and restrictions on Chinese companies.

taxes.summary: Voted for the 2017 tax cuts after pressing for a larger child tax credit.
taxes.source_label: Congress.gov: H.R. 1 (2017), Tax Cuts and Jobs Act

healthcare.summary: Voted for Affordable Care Act repeal efforts in 2017.

guns.summary: Opposes assault-weapons bans; after the 2018 Parkland shooting supported red-flag laws and raising the purchase age for rifles.

energy.summary: Supports expanding U.S. oil and gas production while backing some measures on Florida coastal resilience.

ai.summary: No clear public position found in the seed research.

education.summary: Supports school choice and tax-credit scholarships.

crime.summary: Supports tougher sentencing and increased police funding.

democracy.summary: Opposes adding seats to the Supreme Court and other structural changes to the Court.

candidates.name: Ron DeSantis
candidates.status_note: Has not announced plans for 2028; ran for the 2024 Republican nomination.
candidates.bio: Navy veteran and former congressman, elected governor of Florida in 2018 and re-elected in 2022.

abortion.summary: Signed Florida's 2023 law banning most abortions after six weeks, with limited exceptions; opposed the 2024 ballot measure to expand access.

immigration.summary: Signed a 2023 state law expanding immigration enforcement and has had the state assist federal deportation efforts.

israel.summary: Strong supporter of Israel; said in 2023 the U.S. should not accept refugees from Gaza.

iran.summary: No clear public position found in the seed research.

ukraine.summary: Described the war in 2023 as a 'territorial dispute' that was not a vital U.S. interest, a remark he later qualified.

china_trade.summary: Signed a 2023 law restricting land purchases by Chinese nationals and companies; supports tariffs on China.

taxes.summary: Has pushed state tax cuts and spending restraint, and proposed reducing Florida property taxes.

healthcare.summary: Has opposed Medicaid expansion in Florida.

guns.summary: Signed Florida's 2023 law allowing concealed carry without a permit.

energy.summary: Signed a 2024 law removing most references to climate change from Florida statutes and favoring natural gas; has opposed offshore drilling near Florida.

ai.summary: In late 2025 proposed state protections on AI, including for children and against data centers raising residents' utility bills, and opposed federal preemption of state AI laws.

education.summary: Signed a 2023 law making all Florida students eligible for school vouchers; called for closing the federal Education Department during his 2024 campaign.

crime.summary: Signed 2023 laws allowing the death penalty for child rape and without a unanimous jury.

democracy.summary: Opposes changes to the Supreme Court; created a state office to investigate election crimes.

links.official_label: Office of the Governor of Florida

candidates.name: Ted Cruz
candidates.status_note: Has not ruled out a 2028 run; finished second in the 2016 Republican primaries.
candidates.bio: Former Texas solicitor general, elected to the Senate in 2012; chairs the Senate Commerce Committee.

abortion.summary: Long-time opponent of abortion rights who supported Texas's strict laws; has said since Dobbs that states should lead on the issue.

immigration.summary: Supports border-wall construction and the administration's deportation program.

israel.summary: One of the most outspoken supporters of Israel in Congress; opposes a Palestinian state.

iran.summary: Supported the June 2025 strikes and has spoken in favor of regime change in Iran.

ukraine.summary: Has criticized Russia but opposed large aid packages that did not address the U.S. border.

china_trade.summary: Supports pressure on China but warned in April 2025 that broad tariffs act as a tax on consumers and could cause a recession.

taxes.summary: Has proposed a flat tax and abolishing the IRS; voted for the 2025 budget law.
taxes.source_label: Congress.gov: H.R. 1 (2025), One Big Beautiful Bill Act

healthcare.summary: Led the 2013 effort to defund the Affordable Care Act and supports repealing it.

guns.summary: Opposes new gun restrictions and supports nationwide concealed-carry reciprocity.

energy.summary: Supports maximizing oil and gas production and opposes federal climate regulation.

ai.summary: As Commerce chair in 2025 pushed a federal moratorium on state AI laws and introduced a bill to create a regulatory 'sandbox' for AI companies.

education.summary: Has called for abolishing the federal Department of Education.

crime.summary: Supports tougher sentencing for violent crime and opposes bail reform.

democracy.summary: Proposed a constitutional amendment in 2021 to fix the Supreme Court at nine justices.

candidates.name: Rand Paul
candidates.status_note: Has said publicly he is considering a 2028 run; ran in 2016.
candidates.bio: Ophthalmologist and libertarian-leaning senator, first elected in 2010.

abortion.summary: Has sponsored the Life at Conception Act, which would define legal personhood from conception.

immigration.summary: Supports stronger border enforcement; has been less vocal than some colleagues about mass deportation.

israel.summary: Supports Israel but has long sought to phase out all U.S. foreign aid, including to Israel. This view does not map cleanly onto this scale, so it is not scored.

iran.summary: Voted in June 2025 for a resolution requiring congressional approval for military action against Iran.

ukraine.summary: Has opposed every major Ukraine aid package and voted against the 2024 supplemental.

china_trade.summary: Opposes broad tariffs; voted in April 2025 to end the emergency used to impose tariffs on Canada.

taxes.summary: Favors deep spending cuts and lower taxes; voted against the 2025 budget law because it raised the debt ceiling.
taxes.source_label: Congress.gov: H.R. 1 (2025), One Big Beautiful Bill Act

healthcare.summary: Supports repealing the Affordable Care Act in favor of market-based alternatives.

guns.summary: Opposes federal gun restrictions, including red-flag laws.

energy.summary: Opposes federal climate regulations and clean-energy subsidies.

ai.summary: No clear public position found in the seed research.

education.summary: Supports abolishing the federal Department of Education.

crime.summary: A leading Republican voice for criminal-justice reform: introduced a 2020 bill banning federal no-knock warrants and has sought to end civil asset forfeiture.

democracy.summary: Opposes adding seats to the Supreme Court.
